title: SDK stub-runner usage matrix + failure scenarios (draft)
content:
Context:
This is a lightweight, pragmatic sketch for a small tool we call the 'stub-runner' — a local/CI runner that emulates Redwood SDK edge conditions for integrators and quickstarts. Purpose is to reduce first-call friction, make failure modes visible during onboarding, and give clear remediation guidance so PMs/SEs/customer eng can reproduce issues without needing full infra.

Goals (what success looks like):
- A one-file dev experience that runs minimal flows (auth, generate, embeddings, streaming) with toggles for latency/circuit/partial responses.
- A concise mapping (usage matrix) that tells which SDK entrypoints map to which real-service contract and which emulated failure we exercise.
- A short quickstart that new SDK adopters can run in <5 minutes.
- A set of deterministic failure scenarios with detection signals and simple mitigations documented.

Scope / non-goals:
- Scope: JS + Python SDK ergonomics, CLI invocations used in demos, CI smoke tests. Observability hooks (event names, metrics) included.
- Non-goal: full fidelity to backend runtime; stub focuses on API surface and predictable error shapes.

Primary persona:
- New integrator engineer who wants to prove out an LLM feature without provisioning Redwood Dedicated or private infra.
- Developer Advocate writing a demo that must handle common failure modes.

Usage matrix (entrypoint -> behavior exercised -> quickcheck to run)
- client.generate(text) -> streaming + chunk-drop simulation -> run: stub-runner --flow generate --drop-chunks=0.2
- client.chat(messages) -> tool-calling + function-arg-mismatch -> run: stub-runner --flow chat --tool-schema-mismatch
- client.embed(inputs) -> batch-reordering + transient 429 -> run: stub-runner --flow embed --transient-429=0.15
- client.rerank(items) -> deterministic latency spike -> run: stub-runner --flow rerank --latency-ms=1200
- client.poll(status) -> ephemeral timeout then fallback -> run: stub-runner --flow poll --timeout-behavior=err_then_ok

Quickstart (target: 5 min)
1) prereqs: Node >= 18 or Python 3.10, git, yarn/pip
2) clone tiny repo: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/sdk-stub-runner-example.git && cd sdk-stub-runner-example
3) install deps: yarn && yarn build (or pip install -r requirements.txt)
4) run default stub: ./stub-runner --flow generate
   - expected: a streaming demo that prints tokens every 50ms. If you see a long pause, toggle --drop-chunks=0 to disable chunk drop.
5) run quick fail: ./stub-runner --flow embed --transient-429=1.0
   - expected: client will receive a controlled 429 and retry logic should be visible in logs.
6) run CI smoke: ./stub-runner --ci-smoke (exits 0 if core flows succeed within thresholds)

CLI examples (copy/paste):
- ./stub-runner --flow generate --drop-chunks=0.25 --latency-ms=80
- ./stub-runner --flow chat --tool-schema-mismatch --simulate-truncated-ttls=1
- ./stub-runner --flow embed --batch-size=4 --transient-429=0.2

Failure scenarios (catalog)
1) Transient 429s during embedding uploads
   - Signal: burst of 429s in telemetry, client retries three times then surface error to caller.
   - Stub trigger: --transient-429=PROBABILITY
   - Mitigation: exponential backoff with jitter, fall back to smaller batches (batch-size param), local caching of recent embeddings.

2) Streaming token drop / network blips
   - Signal: missing tokens + partial outputs, client timeouts on streaming connection.
   - Stub trigger: --drop-chunks=PROBABILITY, --chunk-loss-seed=SEED
   - Mitigation: reconcile by requesting last-k prefix or switching to non-streaming path; log and surface partial flag to UX.

3) Function/tool call schema mismatch
   - Signal: LLM emits tool call with unexpected schema; client raises type errors or JSON parse failures.
   - Stub trigger: --tool-schema-mismatch
   - Mitigation: validate tool schemas in SDK at register-time; provide prettified error with example of expected payload.

4) Long-tail latency spikes causing client timeouts
   - Signal: p99 latency > SLO, client circuit-breaker opens.
   - Stub trigger: --latency-ms=N (deterministic), --latency-pattern=spike|sustained
   - Mitigation: increase client timeout, enable fallback model variant or route to dedicated pool, surface user-facing retry hints.

5) Partial completions and early EOF from server
   - Signal: server closes stream with non-zero partial flag; post-validate shows truncated JSON.
   - Stub trigger: --truncate-output=PROBABILITY
   - Mitigation: fallback to deterministic non-streaming generation for critical outputs and log for offline evals.

Observability / telemetry hooks (minimal contract)
- events: ["stub.request.start", "stub.request.end", "stub.error.rate_limited", "stub.stream.chunk_drop", "stub.call.tool_mismatch"]
- metrics (exported for CI checks): stub.requests.count, stub.requests.latency_p50/95/99, stub.errors.429_rate, stub.stream.chunk_loss_rate
- traces: span names should match SDK API names (sdk.generate, sdk.chat, sdk.embed) for easy correlation.

Testing recipes (for QA and Customer Eng):
- Local regression loop: run stub-runner with --ci-smoke, then run quickstart tests in examples/; expect CI to collect metrics and upload to report/ folder.
- Canary for docs: include a short embedded recording (gif) for each CLI run in the docs site; validates steps visually.

Canary rollout plan (docs + SDK):
1) Merge stub-runner into examples repo behind feature flag.
2) Add CI job that runs stub-runner --ci-smoke on push to main; if flakiness > threshold block.
3) Ship docs short-form: 1-page quickstart + failure matrix.
4) After 2 weeks, collect support triage hits tagged stub-runner and iterate.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How close should stub emitted error messages be to production? (parity helps, but leaks internals)
- Should the stub include simple auth simulation (API key check) or lean auth bypass? (we lean bypass for friction)
- Will we maintain the stub in monorepo or separate repo? pros/cons listed in TODOs.

Short TODOs (owner):
- (Aisha) produce trimmed README.md with 5-step quickstart (due 2025-01-21)
- (Marco) add telemetry event definitions to observability schema (GH-PR) (due 2025-01-24)
- (Jen) wire CI smoke job and add flakes guard (JIRA-ENGSDK-1234) (due 2025-02-04)
- (Tariq) add python example with asyncio streaming handler (due 2025-02-01)

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Make the stub importable as a library, not only CLI. Example: from stub_runner import start_local_stub; makes integration tests simpler.
- Consider a tiny web UI for toggling failure knobs during live debugging sessions.

Appendix: quick reproducible checks (copy to terminal)
- git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/sdk-stub-runner-example.git && cd sdk-stub-runner-example
- yarn && yarn start:stub -- --flow chat --tool-schema-mismatch
- python -m examples.run_stub --flow embed --transient-429=0.4

If merged, this doc will be the short narrative for the repo README and the central index for support/test flows. Keep it small, iterate fast, prefer clarity over completeness.
